threads.body: Because the `MessageDigest` instance is reused via `ThreadLocal`, it should be explicitly reset at the start of each digest computation. While `md.digest()` resets state on success, if an IOException (or other runtime exception) happens before `digest()` is called, the `MessageDigest` may retain partial state and corrupt the next checksum computed on the same thread. Fix by calling `md.reset()` at the beginning of the `computeDigest(InputStream, MessageDigest)` method (and preferably ensuring reset happens even on failure).

The new Javadoc is less specific than the previous SHA-1 version and doesn’t describe the output format that callers/tests rely on. Please document that this returns a lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 digest (64 characters), so consumers know how to validate/parse it.

Hex encoding via `new BigInteger(... )` + `String.format(...)` is relatively allocation-heavy and can be a hotspot if many archives are analyzed. Consider switching to a dedicated hex encoder over the digest bytes (e.g., a small local byte-to-hex routine) for lower overhead and clearer intent. This also avoids hard-coding width formatting that would need manual updates if the algorithm changes again.

Could you add a test that verifies the result of this method. Something like
```java
assertThat(toHex("hello".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))).isEqualTo("68656c6c6f");
```
should be enough.
previously the `MessageDigest` was reset at the start of the method. Now it is reset both at the start and end. I think it should be enough to just reset it at the end.
